In 1627, the Bernini family decoded the Baroque lines of a half-sunken boat and carved it into Roman travertine at the foot of the Spanish Steps. Four centuries later, the Fontana della Barcaccia still holds water — and the gesture that built it.

Barcaccia is its private answer. An ergonomic shell that does not merely contain water — it celebrates it as sculptural element. The authority of Italian history, brought into contemporary architecture.
The form embraces the body. The finish tells the story. The technology disappears.
Pietro & Gian Lorenzo Bernini · Piazza di Spagna, Roma

In 1627, Pietro and Gian Lorenzo Bernini carved a half-sunken boat into Roman travertine at the foot of the Spanish Steps. Four centuries later, the Fontana della Barcaccia still holds water — and the gesture that built it.
To enrich the Barcaccia shell, we offer three mosaic methodologies — from geometric rigour to the mastery of the manual cut.
Tesserae laid in a regular grid where each element becomes a pixel of colour. The ideal solution for a contemporary, precise texture — creating dynamic, iridescent chromatic gradients.
Master mosaicists cut each tessera by hand to follow the Baroque curves of the Barcaccia. The organic lines of the sculpture traced with unmatched fluidity — the surface becomes an eternal painting.
Patented tesserae with 24-carat gold leaf sealed between layers of glass for an unalterable luminosity. Available in smooth, undulated, or satin-finished gold.
By Commission: Total customisation of colour, pattern, and technique. If we can lay it by hand, we can lay it for one.

A non-porous engineered material that allows the tub to be realised with invisible seams — appearing as a single block carved from the solid. Silky to the touch, absolute hygiene, and a pristine white that endures unchanged over time.
A celebration of light through tesserae of the highest quality — artistic glass or gold leaf. Laid entirely by hand in our atelier. Tens of thousands of tesserae per piece.
For the most particular commissions, we sculpt the Barcaccia directly from blocks of fine Italian marble using CNC technology. Millimetric precision married to the nobility of natural stone.
Each piece is signed, numbered, and accompanied by a certificate of provenance.
Our technology is not made of screens or unnecessary automation — but of components chosen to last, integrated with the care only a craftsman can guarantee.
Classic hydromassage, airpool, or our microbubble system — engineered for deep, gentle skin treatment. Three technologies, one invisible integration.
An integrated LED system that transforms the bathing ritual into a multisensory experience. Light becomes part of the water.
Jets designed for total concealment or flush integration. The sculptural purity of the lines is maintained without compromising performance.

A penthouse master bath overlooking Riyadh. The Barcaccia set on a bed of white stones, lit from below. The city beyond the glass — the ritual within.

In the second century, Caracalla built a bathing complex for six thousand Romans. The ritual was public, communal, architectural. Thermae reverses the premise — the same circular geometry, the same respect for water and heat, scaled to a private chamber. One body or two.
A solid circular form, freestanding or built-in, designed to be the centre of the room. The technology is more present here — but always in service of real relaxation.
The bath as architecture. The room built around the ritual.

In 216 AD, Caracalla opened the largest bathing complex the ancient world had ever seen. Six thousand Romans bathed simultaneously beneath vaults forty metres high. The ritual was public. The geometry was circular.
Each surface is applied and finished by hand in our atelier. The upper rim finish is fully customisable.
A non-porous mineral composite with invisible seams. Silky to the touch, resistant to time. The purest expression of the circular form.
The decorative language of the Barcaccia extended into a circular form. Vitreous glass or gold-leaf tesserae laid by hand across the full exterior surface.
A textured, mineral micro-resin applied in layers. Warm to the touch, resistant to water and temperature. A modern interpretation of cocciopesto — the ancient Roman waterproof plaster.
By Commission: Total customisation. If we can lay it by hand, we can lay it for one.
Applied in multiple layers by hand. Waterproof, mineral, tactile. A modern surface rooted in the ancient technique of cocciopesto. Improves with age.
High-resistance decorative cement, hand-finished to a raw, architectural texture. Each surface carries the gesture of the hand that made it.
Vitreous glass, gold-leaf, or metallic tesserae — laid by hand across the exterior or along the rim. Pattern and palette to your brief.
Each piece is signed, numbered, and accompanied by a certificate of provenance.
Here the technology is more present — but always in service of real relaxation. Never spectacle.
A fine veil of air that oxygenates the water. No noise. No vibration. Our signature technology — simple, effective, and superior to conventional hydromassage in every measure.
A subtle LED line beneath the rim or at the base. The circular geometry, sculpted in light. The piece appears to float.
Internally insulated structure to maintain water temperature and minimise heat dispersion. Less energy. Longer warmth.
From the Mediterranean shore to private towers on the Arabian Peninsula.
A private spa in a contemporary villa. The Thermae in micro-resin sits at the centre of a vaulted room, framed by oak screens and indirect light. The geometry answers the architecture.
Private inquiries only. No catalogues. No standard options. We respond within seventy-two hours.
